examples.en: The bell had barely rung when the students left the classroom.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{座|すわ}るか{座|すわ}らないかのうちに{寝|ね}てしまった。
examples.en: He fell asleep almost as soon as he sat down.

examples.jp: {雨|あめ}がやんだかやまないかのうちに、{子|こ}どもたちは{外|そと}へ{飛|と}び{出|だ}した。
examples.en: The rain had barely stopped when the kids rushed outside.

quiz.q: {電車|でんしゃ}のドアが{開|ひら}くか＿＿かのうちに、{人|ひと}が{乗|の}り{込|こ}んできた。
quiz.en: The train doors had barely opened when people pushed their way on.

quiz.q: {夏休|なつやす}みが{始|はじ}まるか{始|はじ}まらない＿＿、{宿題|しゅくだい}を{全部|ぜんぶ}{終|お}わらせた。
quiz.en: Almost as soon as summer vacation began, I finished all my homework.

quiz.q: {料理|りょうり}が{出|で}てくるか{出|で}てこないかのうちに、{彼|かれ}は＿＿。
options: {食|た}べ{始|はじ}めてください
{食|た}べ{始|はじ}める{予定|よてい}だ
quiz.en: The food had barely arrived when he started eating.

structure: Verb ている-form / Noun + の + {最中|さいちゅう}に
explain: Something (often unexpected) happens right in the middle of an activity. It is stronger than {間|あいだ}に or {中|ちゅう}. Often used for interruptions.

examples.jp: {会議|かいぎ}の{最中|さいちゅう}に、{電話|でんわ}が{鳴|な}った。
examples.en: In the middle of the meeting, the phone rang.

examples.jp: {食事|しょくじ}をしている{最中|さいちゅう}に、{地震|じしん}が{起|お}きた。
examples.en: An earthquake happened right while we were eating.

examples.jp: {試験|しけん}の{最中|さいちゅう}にお{腹|なか}が{痛|いた}くなった。
examples.en: My stomach started hurting in the middle of the exam.

quiz.q: シャワーを{浴|あ}びている＿＿、お{客|きゃく}さんが{来|き}た。
quiz.en: A guest came while I was in the middle of taking a shower.

quiz.q: {話|はなし}の＿＿に、{寝|ね}ないでください。
quiz.en: Please don't fall asleep in the middle of the talk.

quiz.q: {試合|しあい}の{最中|さいちゅう}に、{雨|あめ}が＿＿。
quiz.en: It started raining in the middle of the match.

structure: Verb dictionary / ている / ない-form, い-adj, な-adj + な, Noun + の + うちに
explain: Do something while a situation lasts, before it changes. "Eat while it's hot." With ない-form, it means "before ~ happens". It can also mean something changed without you noticing.

examples.jp: {温|あたた}かいうちに{食|た}べてください。
examples.en: Please eat it while it's warm.

examples.jp: {若|わか}いうちに、いろいろな{経験|けいけん}をしたほうがいい。
examples.en: You should have many experiences while you're young.

examples.jp: {暗|くら}くならないうちに{帰|かえ}りましょう。
examples.en: Let's go home before it gets dark.

quiz.q: {忘|わす}れない＿＿、メモしておこう。
quiz.en: I'll write it down before I forget.

quiz.q: {日本|にほん}にいる＿＿、{富士山|ふじさん}に{登|のぼ}りたい。
quiz.en: I want to climb Mount Fuji while I'm in Japan.

quiz.q: {話|はな}している＿＿、{仲良|なかよ}くなった。
quiz.en: While we were talking, we became friends.

structure: Verb て-form + {以来|いらい} / Noun + {以来|いらい}
explain: Shows that a situation has continued from a past event until now. The second part shows a state that continues. It is more formal than てから.

examples.jp: {日本|にほん}に{来|き}て{以来|いらい}、{毎日|まいにち}{日本語|にほんご}を{使|つか}っている。
examples.en: Ever since I came to Japan, I've used Japanese every day.

examples.jp: {卒業|そつぎょう}{以来|いらい}、{彼|かれ}とは{会|あ}っていない。
examples.en: I haven't seen him since graduation.

examples.jp: その{事故|じこ}があって{以来|いらい}、{車|くるま}に{乗|の}るのが{怖|こわ}い。
examples.en: Ever since that accident, I've been scared of riding in cars.

quiz.q: {犬|いぬ}を{飼|か}い{始|はじ}めて＿＿、{毎朝|まいあさ}{散歩|さんぽ}している。
quiz.en: Ever since I started keeping a dog, I've gone for a walk every morning.

quiz.q: {入社|にゅうしゃ}＿＿、{一度|いちど}も{休|やす}んだことがない。
quiz.en: I haven't taken a single day off since I joined the company.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}とけんかして＿＿、{話|はな}していない。
quiz.en: I haven't talked to her since we had a fight.

meaning: taking ~ as a chance; ~ led to
structure: Noun / plain form + の + をきっかけに(して)
explain: Shows the event that started a change or a new action. "A trip to Japan got me interested in Japanese." It is common for life changes.

examples.jp: {旅行|りょこう}をきっかけに、{日本語|にほんご}の{勉強|べんきょう}を{始|はじ}めた。
examples.en: A trip got me started studying Japanese.

examples.jp: {病気|びょうき}をきっかけに、たばこをやめた。
examples.en: Getting sick made me quit smoking.

examples.jp: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しをきっかけにして、{新|あたら}しい{家具|かぐ}を{買|か}った。
examples.en: I took the move as a chance to buy new furniture.

quiz.q: {留学|りゅうがく}＿＿、{世界|せかい}に{興味|きょうみ}を{持|も}つようになった。
quiz.en: Studying abroad got me interested in the world.

quiz.q: この{映画|えいが}＿＿、{歴史|れきし}が{好|す}きになった。
quiz.en: This movie made me start liking history.

quiz.q: {結婚|けっこん}＿＿、{料理|りょうり}を{習|なら}い{始|はじ}めた。
quiz.en: Getting married was what made me start learning to cook.

structure: Noun + を{契機|けいき}に(して) / を{契機|けいき}として
explain: A formal version of をきっかけに. It is used for big events in society, business or life, and often appears in news and essays.

examples.jp: {震災|しんさい}を{契機|けいき}に、{防災|ぼうさい}への{関心|かんしん}が{高|たか}まった。
examples.en: The earthquake disaster led to more interest in disaster prevention.

examples.jp: {転職|てんしょく}を{契機|けいき}として、{東京|とうきょう}に{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}した。
examples.en: Changing jobs was my turning point to move to Tokyo.

examples.jp: オリンピックを{契機|けいき}に、{町|まち}が{大|おお}きく{変|か}わった。
examples.en: The Olympics marked a big change for the city.

quiz.q: {会社|かいしゃ}の{合併|がっぺい}＿＿、{組織|そしき}が{見直|みなお}された。
quiz.en: The company merger served as a chance to review the organization.

quiz.q: {事故|じこ}＿＿、{安全|あんぜん}{対策|たいさく}が{強化|きょうか}された。
quiz.en: Following the accident, safety measures were strengthened.

quiz.q: {退職|たいしょく}＿＿、{田舎|いなか}で{暮|く}らし{始|はじ}めた。
quiz.en: Retirement was the turning point for me to start living in the countryside.

meaning: for ~; to ~ (from someone's point of view)
structure: Noun + にとって / にとっての + Noun
explain: Shows from whose point of view something is judged, like "for me, this is important". The second part is usually a judgment or evaluation. Compare に{対|たい}して, which shows the target of an action.

examples.jp: {私|わたし}にとって、{家族|かぞく}が{一番|いちばん}{大切|たいせつ}です。
examples.en: For me, family is the most important thing.

examples.jp: {子|こ}どもにとって、{遊|あそ}びは{勉強|べんきょう}と{同|おな}じぐらい{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.en: For children, play is as important as study.

examples.jp: この{写真|しゃしん}は{彼|かれ}にとっての{宝物|たからもの}だ。
examples.en: This photo is a treasure to him.

quiz.q: {外国人|がいこくじん}＿＿、{漢字|かんじ}は{難|むずか}しい。
quiz.en: For foreigners, kanji is difficult.

quiz.q: {学生|がくせい}＿＿、{夏休|なつやす}みは{楽|たの}しみだ。
quiz.en: For students, summer vacation is something to look forward to.

quiz.q: この{仕事|しごと}は{私|わたし}＿＿{大|おお}きなチャンスだ。
quiz.en: This job is a big chance for me.

structure: Noun + として / としての + Noun
explain: Shows a role, position or status: "as a teacher", "as a gift". としては can mean "for a ~". Compare にとって, which shows whose point of view.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{通訳|つうやく}として{働|はたら}いている。
examples.en: He works as an interpreter.

examples.jp: {親|おや}としての{責任|せきにん}がある。
examples.en: I have responsibilities as a parent.

examples.jp: このお{寺|てら}は{世界|せかい}{遺産|いさん}として{登録|とうろく}された。
examples.en: This temple was registered as a World Heritage site.

quiz.q: {留学生|りゅうがくせい}＿＿{日本|にほん}に{来|き}ました。
quiz.en: I came to Japan as an international student.

quiz.q: {社会人|しゃかいじん}＿＿のマナーを{学|まな}ぶ。
quiz.en: I'm learning manners as a working adult.

quiz.q: これはお{土産|みやげ}＿＿{人気|にんき}がある。
quiz.en: This is popular as a souvenir.

structure: Noun + によって / による + Noun
explain: Has several uses: who did something in passive sentences, "depending on" (people differ), the means, or the cause. It is common in formal writing. Compare に{応|おう}じて, which means adjusting to match.

examples.jp: この{絵|え}はピカソによって{描|か}かれた。
examples.en: This painting was painted by Picasso.

examples.jp: {人|ひと}によって{考|かんが}え{方|かた}が{違|ちが}う。
examples.en: Ways of thinking differ from person to person.

examples.jp: {台風|たいふう}による{被害|ひがい}が{大|おお}きかった。
examples.en: The damage caused by the typhoon was severe.

quiz.q: {国|くに}＿＿、{習慣|しゅうかん}が{違|ちが}います。
quiz.en: Customs differ depending on the country.

quiz.q: この{建物|たてもの}は{有名|ゆうめい}な{建築家|けんちくか}＿＿{設計|せっけい}された。
quiz.en: This building was designed by a famous architect.

quiz.q: {地震|じしん}＿＿{電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まった。
quiz.en: The trains stopped because of the earthquake.

structure: Verb た-form / Noun + の + {上|うえ}で
explain: Do one thing first, and then do the next thing based on it. "Read it carefully, then sign." It is often used for careful decisions and procedures.

examples.jp: よく{考|かんが}えた{上|うえ}で、{返事|へんじ}をします。
examples.en: I'll answer after thinking it over carefully.

examples.jp: {家族|かぞく}と{相談|そうだん}の{上|うえ}で、{決|き}めます。
examples.en: I'll decide after talking it over with my family.

examples.jp: {内容|ないよう}を{確認|かくにん}した{上|うえ}で、サインしてください。
examples.en: Please sign after checking the contents.

quiz.q: {実際|じっさい}に{見|み}た＿＿、{買|か}うかどうか{決|き}めたい。
quiz.en: I want to decide whether to buy it after actually seeing it.

quiz.q: {説明|せつめい}をよく{聞|き}いた＿＿、{申|もう}し{込|こ}んでください。
quiz.en: Please apply after listening carefully to the explanation.

quiz.q: {話|はな}し{合|あ}いの＿＿、{計画|けいかく}を{変更|へんこう}した。
quiz.en: We changed the plan after discussing it.

meaning: on the other hand; while ~ (two sides)
structure: plain form + {反面|はんめん} (な-adj + な / である)
explain: Shows that one thing has two opposite sides, one good and one bad. "City life is convenient, but expensive." Compare {一方|いっぽう}で, which can compare two different things.

examples.jp: {都会|とかい}の{生活|せいかつ}は{便利|べんり}な{反面|はんめん}、お{金|かね}がかかる。
examples.en: City life is convenient, but on the other hand it's expensive.

examples.jp: この{仕事|しごと}は{大変|たいへん}な{反面|はんめん}、やりがいがある。
examples.en: This job is hard, but it's also rewarding.

examples.jp: スマホは{便利|べんり}な{反面|はんめん}、{使|つか}いすぎると{目|め}に{悪|わる}い。
examples.en: Smartphones are convenient, but using them too much is bad for your eyes.

quiz.q: {一人|ひとり}{暮|ぐ}らしは{自由|じゆう}な＿＿、さびしいこともある。
quiz.en: Living alone is free, but it can also be lonely.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は{厳|きび}しい＿＿、{優|やさ}しいところもある。
quiz.en: He's strict, but he also has a kind side.

quiz.q: この{薬|くすり}はよく{効|き}く＿＿、{副作用|ふくさよう}が{強|つよ}い。
quiz.en: This medicine works well, but its side effects are strong.

structure: Verb dictionary form + {一方|いっぽう}だ
explain: Shows that a situation keeps moving in one direction, often a bad one: "prices keep rising". The verb shows change, like {増|ふ}える, {悪|わる}くなる, {減|へ}る.

examples.jp: {物価|ぶっか}は{上|あ}がる{一方|いっぽう}だ。
examples.en: Prices just keep going up.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}の{病気|びょうき}は{悪|わる}くなる{一方|いっぽう}だ。
examples.en: His illness keeps getting worse.

examples.jp: この{町|まち}の{人口|じんこう}は{減|へ}る{一方|いっぽう}です。
examples.en: This town's population keeps decreasing.

quiz.q: {仕事|しごと}が{増|ふ}える＿＿で、{休|やす}む{時間|じかん}がない。
quiz.en: My work keeps increasing, and I have no time to rest.

quiz.q: {雨|あめ}は{強|つよ}くなる＿＿。
quiz.en: The rain keeps getting heavier.

quiz.q: {日本|にほん}に{来|く}る{観光客|かんこうきゃく}は{増|ふ}える＿＿。
quiz.en: The number of tourists coming to Japan keeps growing.

structure: Verb ます-stem + つつある
explain: Shows that a change is happening now, step by step. It is written style, used in news and reports. It is like ている for change, but stresses the ongoing process.

examples.jp: {景気|けいき}は{回復|かいふく}しつつある。
examples.en: The economy is in the process of recovering.

examples.jp: {地球|ちきゅう}の{温度|おんど}は{上|あ}がりつつある。
examples.en: The Earth's temperature is steadily rising.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}のけがは{少|すこ}しずつ{治|なお}りつつある。
examples.en: His injury is gradually healing.

quiz.q: {古|ふる}い{習慣|しゅうかん}は{消|き}え＿＿。
quiz.en: Old customs are gradually disappearing.

quiz.q: {新|あたら}しい{技術|ぎじゅつ}が{広|ひろ}まり＿＿。
quiz.en: New technology is spreading.

quiz.q: {町|まち}は{少|すこ}しずつ{変|か}わり＿＿。
quiz.en: The town is gradually changing.

structure: Verb た-form / い-adj / な-adj + な + ことに
explain: Shows the speaker's feeling about the following fact first: "Surprisingly, ..." or "Sadly, ...". It is used with feeling words like {驚|おどろ}いた, {残念|ざんねん}な, うれしい.

examples.jp: {驚|おどろ}いたことに、{彼|かれ}は{一人|ひとり}で{全部|ぜんぶ}やった。
examples.en: Surprisingly, he did it all by himself.

examples.jp: {残念|ざんねん}なことに、{雨|あめ}で{花火|はなび}が{中止|ちゅうし}になった。
examples.en: Sadly, the fireworks were cancelled due to rain.

examples.jp: うれしいことに、{試験|しけん}に{合格|ごうかく}した。
examples.en: Happily, I passed the exam.

quiz.q: {不思議|ふしぎ}な＿＿、{誰|だれ}もその{音|おと}を{聞|き}いていなかった。
quiz.en: Strangely, nobody had heard that sound.

quiz.q: ありがたい＿＿、たくさんの{人|ひと}が{手伝|てつだ}ってくれた。
quiz.en: Thankfully, many people helped me.

quiz.q: {悲|かな}しい＿＿、その{店|みせ}は{閉店|へいてん}してしまった。
quiz.en: Sadly, that shop has closed.

structure: Verb dictionary form / い-adj / な-adj + な + ものがある
explain: Expresses a strong feeling the speaker gets from something: "There's something moving about his speech." It is used with words about feelings and impressions.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}の{歌|うた}には、{心|こころ}に{響|ひび}くものがある。
examples.en: There's something about his songs that touches the heart.

examples.jp: {一人|ひとり}で{海外|かいがい}に{住|す}むのは、さびしいものがある。
examples.en: There's something lonely about living abroad alone.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}の{演技|えんぎ}には{素晴|すば}らしいものがある。
examples.en: There's something wonderful about her acting.

quiz.q: {子|こ}どもの{成長|せいちょう}の{速|はや}さには、{驚|おどろ}く＿＿。
quiz.en: There's something amazing about how fast children grow.

quiz.q: この{景色|けしき}には{感動|かんどう}させる＿＿。
quiz.en: There's something moving about this scenery.

quiz.q: {毎日|まいにち}{同|おな}じ{仕事|しごと}を{続|つづ}けるのは、つらい＿＿。
quiz.en: There's something hard about doing the same work every day.

structure: Verb ない-stem + ずに{済|す}む / Verb ない-form + なくて{済|す}む
explain: Shows that you were able to avoid something you thought you'd have to do, often with relief. "Luckily I didn't have to pay." Compare ざるを{得|え}ない, which means you have no choice but to do it.

examples.jp: {友達|ともだち}が{車|くるま}で{送|おく}ってくれたので、{歩|ある}かずに{済|す}んだ。
examples.en: My friend drove me, so I didn't have to walk.

examples.jp: {早|はや}く{見|み}つかったので、{手術|しゅじゅつ}をせずに{済|す}んだ。
examples.en: It was found early, so I didn't need surgery.

examples.jp: {電話|でんわ}で{説明|せつめい}できたので、{行|い}かなくて{済|す}んだ。
examples.en: I could explain by phone, so I didn't have to go.

quiz.q: {先輩|せんぱい}が{教|おし}えてくれたので、{失敗|しっぱい}せ＿＿。
options: ずにはいられなかった
quiz.en: My senior taught me, so I managed to avoid failing.

quiz.q: {雨|あめ}がやんだので、{傘|かさ}を{買|か}わ＿＿。
options: ずにはいられなかった
quiz.en: The rain stopped, so I didn't have to buy an umbrella.

quiz.q: {近|ちか}くに{住|す}めば、{電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}ら＿＿。
quiz.en: If you live nearby, you won't have to take the train.

structure: Noun / Verb dictionary form + に{先立|さきだ}って / に{先立|さきだ}つ + Noun
explain: Shows something done before an important event, as preparation. It is formal and used for ceremonies, events and business. Compare {前|まえ}に, which is everyday and neutral.

examples.jp: {試合|しあい}に{先立|さきだ}って、{開会式|かいかいしき}が{行|おこな}われた。
examples.en: An opening ceremony was held before the match.

examples.jp: {出発|しゅっぱつ}に{先立|さきだ}って、{注意|ちゅうい}{事項|じこう}を{説明|せつめい}します。
examples.en: Before departure, I'll explain the precautions.

examples.jp: {映画|えいが}の{公開|こうかい}に{先立|さきだ}つ{試写会|ししゃかい}に{招待|しょうたい}された。
examples.en: I was invited to a preview screening before the movie's release.

quiz.q: {工事|こうじ}を{始|はじ}める＿＿、{住民|じゅうみん}に{説明|せつめい}した。
quiz.en: Before starting construction, they explained it to the residents.

quiz.q: {新商品|しんしょうひん}の{発売|はつばい}＿＿、{記者|きしゃ}{会見|かいけん}が{開|ひら}かれた。
quiz.en: Before the new product went on sale, a press conference was held.

quiz.q: {留学|りゅうがく}＿＿、ビザを{取|と}らなければならない。
quiz.en: Before studying abroad, you have to get a visa.

structure: Noun + に{反|はん}して / に{反|はん}する + Noun
explain: Shows that a result is the opposite of what was expected, hoped or planned. Common with {予想|よそう}, {期待|きたい}, {意志|いし}. It can also mean "against" a rule.

examples.jp: {予想|よそう}に{反|はん}して、{試験|しけん}は{簡単|かんたん}だった。
examples.en: Contrary to expectations, the exam was easy.

examples.jp: {親|おや}の{期待|きたい}に{反|はん}して、{彼|かれ}は{大学|だいがく}に{行|い}かなかった。
examples.en: Against his parents' hopes, he didn't go to university.

examples.jp: それは{規則|きそく}に{反|はん}する{行為|こうい}だ。
examples.en: That is an act against the rules.

quiz.q: みんなの{予想|よそう}＿＿、{弱|よわ}いチームが{勝|か}った。
quiz.en: Contrary to everyone's predictions, the weak team won.

quiz.q: {本人|ほんにん}の{意志|いし}＿＿、{彼|かれ}は{転勤|てんきん}させられた。
quiz.en: He was transferred against his own will.

quiz.q: {天気|てんき}{予報|よほう}＿＿、{一日中|いちにちじゅう}{晴|は}れていた。
quiz.en: Contrary to the weather forecast, it was sunny all day.

structure: plain form / Noun + というより(も) (な-adj: no だ)
explain: Corrects or refines a description: "It's not so much A, it's more B." Often followed by むしろ. It is common in conversation.

examples.jp: {今日|きょう}は{暖|あたた}かいというより{暑|あつ}い。
examples.en: Today isn't so much warm as hot.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{先生|せんせい}というより{友達|ともだち}みたいだ。
examples.en: He's more like a friend than a teacher.

examples.jp: これは{料理|りょうり}というより、{芸術|げいじゅつ}だ。
examples.en: This is less a dish than a work of art.

quiz.q: この{部屋|へや}は{静|しず}か＿＿、さびしい{感|かん}じだ。
quiz.en: This room feels lonely rather than quiet.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}は{歌|うた}が{上手|じょうず}＿＿プロのようだ。
quiz.en: She's not just good at singing; she's like a professional.

quiz.q: {疲|つか}れた＿＿、もう{眠|ねむ}くて{動|うご}けない。
quiz.en: I'm beyond tired; I'm so sleepy I can't move.

meaning: although I say ~; even though it's ~
structure: plain form / Noun + といっても
explain: Corrects what people might expect from a word: "I said I traveled, but it was just one night." It lowers expectations. Compare というより, which corrects the description itself.

examples.jp: {料理|りょうり}ができるといっても、{簡単|かんたん}なものだけです。
examples.en: I can cook, but only simple things.

examples.jp: {旅行|りょこう}といっても、{近|ちか}くの{温泉|おんせん}に{一泊|いっぱく}しただけだ。
examples.en: I say "trip", but I just stayed one night at a nearby hot spring.

examples.jp: {社長|しゃちょう}といっても、{社員|しゃいん}は{三人|さんにん}だけです。
examples.en: I'm the president, but there are only three employees.

quiz.q: {日本語|にほんご}が{話|はな}せる＿＿、{日常会話|にちじょうかいわ}{程度|ていど}です。
quiz.en: I can speak Japanese, but only at an everyday conversation level.

quiz.q: {庭|にわ}がある＿＿、とても{小|ちい}さいです。
quiz.en: There's a garden, but it's very small.

quiz.q: {忙|いそが}しい＿＿、{少|すこ}しは{休|やす}む{時間|じかん}もある。
quiz.en: I'm busy, but I do have a little time to rest.
